newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trust banks slip on S'tomo Trust jitters.
newsitem.headline: Japan trust banks slip on S'tomo Trust jitters.

text.p: Shares in Japanese trust banks slipped across the board on Wednesday on jitters triggered by news that the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) had suspended shares in Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, traders said.

Trade in Sumitomo Trust's shares was halted for the entire session starting from 0135 GMT amid rumours that the trust bank was considering equity financing. Sumitomo Trust later called a news conference at which it denied rumours that it has suffered large foreign exchange losses and that is withdrawing from overseas business. It also said it is considering financing but that the timing and the amount were undecided.
At 0502 GMT, shares in Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd had lost 58 yen to stand at 902, making it the second steepest percentage loser on the first section of the TSE.
Nippon Trust Bank Ltd fell 20 yen to 380, ranking as the seventh biggest loser.
Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd was down 20 yen at 890, while Mitsubishi Trust & Banking Corp fell 20 yen to 1,580 and Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd shed 28 yen to trade at 686.
